data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Integer maps are deterministic, unlike physical noise.","Kolmogorov complexity is generally non-computable."],"overturn_conditions":["Discovery of a cycle where base-3 complexity is preserved."],"shared_structure":["Interaction between disparate bases","Complexity reduction over time","Attractor states"],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_008","SCR_004"],"transfer_claims":["The process of reaching 1 is analogous to the erasure of a structured signal by white noise."]},"claim":"The Collatz conjecture is unsettled, but it is fundamentally a problem of 'base-representation erasure' where the 3n+1 map acts as a noise source that destroys base-3 structure in favor of base-2 convergence.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The existence of an integer n whose base-3 structure is 'self-healing' under the (3n+1)/2 map.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Proof that base-3 complexity can increase monotonically for a subset of integers.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'covering principle' is the systematic reduction of the Kolmogorov complexity of n when expressed in base 3, as the interleaved operations of multiplication by 3 (shifting base-3 digits) and division by 2 (introducing base-2 noise) force the sequence toward the simplest base-2 state (1).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
